podcast.title: MC for Richie Valens Memorial Concert
podcast.body: Run Holden served as the master of ceremonies for the Richie Valens Memorial Concert, which famously featured The Beach Boys' first major professional live performance. "Holdin' was also the MC for the Richie Vance Memorial concert, which was the Beach Boys' first major professional live performance."

podcast.title: Most Popular Band in Seattle
podcast.body: Run Holden led The Thunderbirds, which was the most popular band in the Seattle area during his time there. "One holdin' led the most popular band in the Seattle area, the Thunderbirds"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Move to Los Angeles
podcast.body: Following the pattern of many successful Seattle musicians, Run Holden moved to Los Angeles after achieving a hit with "Love You So" but no subsequent chart success. "But as every musician from Seattle who had any success did, he moved away. He moved to LA"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Second Generation Musician
podcast.body: Run Holden was a second-generation musician, whose father, Oscar Holden, was known as the "father of Seattle Jazz" and had performed with legendary figures like Louis Armstrong and Jelly Roll Morton. "In fact, he was a second generation musician. His father, Oscar Holdin, was known as the father of Seattle Jazz, and had played with both Louis Armstrong and Jelly Roll Morton."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Simplified "Louie Louie" Arrangement
podcast.body: Run Holden's saxophone player, Carlos Ward, created a crucial, guitar-friendly arrangement for "Louie Louie," simplifying Richard Berry's complex second inversion major 7th chord to a simpler minor 5 chord. This arrangement became the standard for nearly all subsequent covers in the Pacific Northwest, as bands learned it from Holden's live performances rather than Berry's original. "Holdin, or rather his saxophone player Carlos Ward, who did the Thunderbirds arrangements, had made a crucial change to Louis Louis, one that made it simpler to play on the guitar, and thus suitable for the guitar heavy music that was starting to predominate in the Pacific Northwest."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
